page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-384-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance designed for massive data footprints and intensive I/O operations. Built on x86_64 architecture, this instance features 384 dedicated vCPUs alongside 3024.0 GB of system memory, delivering approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

A central feature of the z4d-highmem-384-standardlssd configuration is its bundled local storage array. The machine is provisioned with 90194 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity spread across 24 local solid-state drives. This large-scale, direct-attached NVMe storage pool provides low-latency disk access and high throughput directly on the host, avoiding network storage bottlenecks for high-frequency read and write cycles.

Resource allocation is balanced between substantial memory capacity and immense local NVMe bandwidth. The high-density hardware allocation aggregates substantial compute and memory resources onto a single instance, making it cost-efficient for consolidating multiple database nodes or handling enterprise-scale in-memory tables that require direct local persistence. However, users must account for the ephemeral nature of direct-attached local NVMe arrays, which necessitate application-level data redundancy.

The z4d-highmem-384-standardlssd instance is suited for massive transactional databases, distributed NoSQL clusters, real-time log analytics, large-scale data warehousing, and high-throughput data processing pipelines requiring rapid access to dozens of terabytes of hot data.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-384-standardlssd is a storage-optimized instance engineered for extreme I/O and large-scale data processing workloads. Based on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 384 dedicated vCPUs and 3024.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a high memory density of 7.88 GB per virtual core. The platform features an extensive bundled storage capacity of 90194 GB spread across 24 local NVMe SSDs, providing ultra-low latency and high data throughput for local storage operations. The system operates without dedicated GPU hardware and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dense combination of compute, memory, and fast local NVMe makes this instance cost-effective for consolidating infrastructure that would otherwise require multiple separate hosts. It is particularly matched for high-throughput transactional databases, large NoSQL clusters, distributed analytics engines, and enterprise ETL pipelines that require massive local storage arrays.
